Finding: Training dataset contains 6,289 Benign images (52.94%) and 5,590 Malignant images (47.06%).
Research_Implication: The training dataset is relatively balanced; severe class imbalance is not present.

Finding: Test dataset contains 1,000 Benign and 1,000 Malignant images.
Research_Implication: The test dataset is perfectly balanced.

Finding: Both classes show substantial variation in lesion size, shape, pigmentation, texture, surrounding skin, illumination, and acquisition conditions.
Research_Implication: The dataset contains substantial intra-class visual variation.

Finding: Some Benign and Malignant images have visually similar general characteristics.
Research_Implication: Classification cannot be assumed to depend on one simple visual feature.

Finding: Some images contain hairs, measurement markings, circular dermoscopic fields, and varying backgrounds.
Research_Implication: Preprocessing and augmentation should account for acquisition-related variation.

Finding: All analyzed training images are 224×224 pixels with an aspect ratio of 1.0.
Research_Implication: Images already have a standardized spatial resolution.

Finding: Benign images generally have higher mean brightness, while Malignant images are generally shifted toward lower brightness. Considerable overlap remains.
Research_Implication: Brightness is a dataset-level characteristic and should not be treated as a standalone diagnostic feature.

Finding: Malignant images show a broader distribution of pixel-intensity variation than Benign images.
Research_Implication: Normalization and augmentation may help the models handle acquisition variation.

Finding: RGB channel means differ between the two classes, particularly in the Red channel.
Research_Implication: Color characteristics may provide useful information, but may also reflect dataset/acquisition bias.

Finding: IQR analysis identified statistical outliers in brightness, contrast, and RGB statistics.
Research_Implication: Statistical outlier status alone is insufficient justification for removing an image.

Finding: Representative extreme images were visually inspected and were found to be valid dermoscopic images rather than clearly corrupted images.
Research_Implication: No images should be removed solely because they are statistical outliers.

Finding: No exact train-test duplicates were identified using exact image hashing.
Research_Implication: No evidence of exact train-test image duplication was found.

Finding: Highly similar pHash candidates were identified; the strongest candidates were manually inspected and no visually identical or near-identical pairs were observed among the inspected samples.
Research_Implication: No apparent train-test leakage was identified through the conducted duplicate/near-duplicate checks.
